public_rationale: Prominent early reactions were indeed harsh: Howard warned of deep trouble, and Ars criticized marginal gains and poor coding value. But the broader reception was not uniformly brutal. Karpathy was qualified and enthusiastic, while Every described disappointment followed by appreciation. The harsh-reaction component holds; the generalization about early reviews overstates the consistency of their tone.
limitations: This is a qualitative assessment of a small, varied sample, not a measured majority.
Reading the statement only as a description of Marcus's selected examples would favor support.
Every's accessible article was updated after the launch period.
